title: Transduction and Expansion of Primary T Cells in Nine Days with Maintenance of Central Memory Phenotype
protocol: Plate 293T cells for transfection in Dulbecco's modified Eagle medium (DMEM) + 10% fetal bovine serum (FBS) without antibiotics.
Allow the cells to grow overnight at 37 °C before transfection.
Dilute 60 μL of transfection reagent in 1.5 mL reduced serum media.
Incubate for 5 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare a tube containing 1.5 mL of reduced serum media and the following plasmids: 9.0 μg of a transfer plasmid, 3 μg of RD114, and 1.2 μg of VSV-G.
Add diluted plasmids to diluted transfection reagent.
Mix gently.
Incubate for 20 minutes at room temperature.
Feed cells with 5 mL of fresh complete media.
Add 3 mL of transfection reagent/plasmid mixture dropwise per flask.
Incubate for 5–6 hours at 37 °C.
Add an additional 5 mL of fresh medium to the flasks.
Incubate for 42–43 hours at 37 °C.
Collect media after a total transfection time of 48 hours.
Centrifuge at 1282 x g for 3 minutes at 4 °C to remove cell debris.
Aliquot into appropriate volumes for future use.
Flash freeze the virus in an ethanol/dry ice bath.
Store at -80 °C.
Add the virus to the corresponding well and swirl gently to mix.
Incubate for 48 h at 37 °C.
Trypsinize the 293T cells by adding 0.5 mL of Trypsin-EDTA and incubating for 4 min at 37 °C.
Stop the trypsin by adding 1.5 mL of DMEM + 10% FBS.
Count the cells and determine viability with an automated cell counter or a hemocytometer.
Add 10 µL of cells to 10 µL of trypan blue, mix, load the chamber slide, and insert into the counter.
Push the "capture" button to count the cells.
Collect 0.5–1 x 10^6 cells and evaluate levels of CAR and CXCR5 by flow cytometry.
Calculate viral titer using the sample with a transduction level of 20% or less.
Use the formula: transduction units/mL = (number of cells in culture)(% of cells transduced)/volume of virus added to the culture.
Choose a concentration of virus that allows maximal transduction without loss of cell viability.
Dilute anti-macaque CD3 antibody (FN18) stock to 10 µg/mL in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dispense 2 mL/well in 6-well plates.
Incubate at 37 °C for 2 h or overnight at 4 °C.
Aspirate PBS and unbound antibodies from the wells.
Rinse wells twice with 2 mL of PBS.
Thaw primary rhesus PBMCs in a 37 °C waterbath until just a small amount of ice remains.
Gently pipette cells into a conical tube.
Rinse the vial with 1 mL of basic medium and add it slowly to the cells.
Add an additional 9 mL of warm basic medium to the cells.
Centrifuge at 600 x g for 5 min at 22 °C to pellet the cells.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in a small amount of growth medium.
Stain cells with trypan blue and count the cells.
Add 10 μL of cells to 10 μL trypan blue for cell counting.
Mix the cell and trypan blue solution thoroughly.
Load the mixed solution into the chamber slide of an automated cell counter.
Insert the chamber slide into the cell counter.
Push the "capture" button to count the cells using the cell counter.
Calculate the total number of cells by multiplying the cell concentration by volume.
Dilute the cells to 2 x 10^6 cells/mL in growth medium.
Add anti-CD28 to a final concentration of 5 μg/ml for T cell activation.
Pipette cells into anti-CD3 coated plates.
Incubate the plates with cells at 37 °C in 5% CO2 for 2 days.
Prepare fibronectin reagent by diluting it 1:100 in sterile PBS.
Pipette 2 mL of sterile fibronectin solution into each well of a 6-well plate.
Gently rock the plates for 2 h at room temperature to coat them with fibronectin.
Remove the fibronectin solution by aspiration from each well.
Block the coated wells with 1 mL of sterile 2% bovine serum albumin (BSA, Fraction V) in PBS.
Rock the plates at room temperature for 30 min.
Aspirate the BSA solution and wash the plate with 2 mL of PBS.
Wash the fibronectin-coated plates by aspirating PBS after washing.
Seal the fibronectin-coated plates with seal wrap and store at 4°C for up to a week.
Warm a centrifuge to 32°C by running at 2000 x g for about 30 min.
Warm serum-free medium in a 37°C water bath.
Warm growth media in a 37°C water bath.
Thaw the virus on ice or gently swirl the vial in a 37°C water bath until only small amounts of ice remain.
Dilute the retrovirus to an optimal multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 0.5 in serum-free medium.
Pellet the cells in the tubes by centrifuging at 600 x g for 5 min at 32°C.
Aspirate the media from the cell pellet.
Resuspend the cells in growth medium at a concentration of 1.5 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Add 1 mL of cell suspension to each virus-coated well, containing 2 mL growth medium per well.
Centrifuge the plates at 1000 x g for 10 min at 32°C.
Incubate the plates for 48 h at 37°C under 5% CO2.
Draw the contents of the wells up and down with a 5 mL pipet to resuspend the cells.
Transfer the contents to a 50 mL conical tube.
Add 1 mL of growth media to each well and draw up and down with a sterile transfer pipet to remove adherent cells.
Count cells to determine the total cell number and viability using an automated cell counter.
If desired, remove 1 x 10^6 cells for flow cytometry to assess gene expression and phenotype.
Centrifuge the cells at 600 x g for 10 min at 25°C.
Aspirate the media from the cells.
Resuspend the cells in expansion media at a concentration of 1 x 10^6 cells/mL.
Seed each gas-permeable well of a 6-well plate with 5 mL of resuspended cells.
Layer an additional 25 mL of expansion media per well to ensure the cells remain on the bottom of the well.
Incubate the cells undisturbed at 37 °C in a 5% CO2 incubator for 4 days.
Remove and discard 20 mL of media from each gas permeable well, being careful not to disturb the cells.
Rinse each well with 3 mL of media to collect any residual cells if additional culture days are desired.
Pipette the remaining media up and down to dislodge the cells; the media should appear cloudy if cell growth is adequate.
Count the collected cells using an automated counter or a hemocytometer to assess viability and number.
Perform flow cytometry to determine transduced gene expression and cell phenotype.
Determine rhesus macaque PBMC phenotype using antibodies directed against CD4, CD3, CD8, CD95, CD28, CXCR5, and MBL.
Assess viability with a fixable viability dye.
Prepare cells for flow cytometry.
Make up an antibody master mix for the total number of tubes.
Bring up to total volume using PBS.
Add 0.5–1 x 10^6 cells per tube.
Include negative controls such as unstained cells and stained mock transduced cells.
Add 2 ml of PBS to the cells, centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at room temperature (RT), and decant.
Add 100 μl of antibody mix to the tubes and incubate for 30 min at RT.
Add 2 ml of PBS, centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at RT, and decant.
Add 300 μl of 1% paraformaldehyde and incubate for 15 min.
Centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 min at RT and decant.
Add 300 μl of PBS and mix.
Acquire 150,000 events for each sample on a flow cytometer.
Analyze the data with flow analysis software.
